title: Looking for Recommendations of Culturally Significant Films

commenti.body: For the last few years I’ve been working my way through a similar list with my son. It’s been a blast. He left for college this year, but we’re still knocking the occasional film off the list when he’s back. It’s too long to post here, but if you’re interested just DM me, and I can send you a link to the Google sheet.

As a kid I liked that my parents would just let us rent anything then go to bed. I’d hand a video to my mom and she’d go, “Oh flowers, in an attic, I love flowers!” Amityville Horror, Fatal Attraction, Friday the 13th, Friday the 13th II, Truth or Dare, Whatever Happened to Baby Jane, Sunset Boulevard, Vertigo, The Toxic Avenger. My mother’s English wasn’t great and we actually got to rent Striptease. It’s a bad film but being the only kid to see in 6th grade was pretty rad. I had to wait until I was an adult to see Basic Instinct because mom saw on tv the outrage. “You no get this! Woman open legs movie!”

Rocky is pretty iconic and should be up there. Before it got saturated, Titanic was a cultural beast. Silence of the Lambs (depending on how you think your kids would do with it, since it has some graphic moments), Forest Gump, Do the Right Thing, Citizen Kane, and Good Will Hunting all come to mind.
These are all great. I can't believe I forgot about some of these. Thank you.

Basically, if you got a list of movies that are parodied in the first 10 seasons of The Simpsons, that would function as a good list of movies that people are culturally aware of (at least, pre-1990s)

This is a great rec as I am trying to do kind of the same thing with my daughter. 

Ignoring ratings I would have these on the list: 

* The Matrix
* Indiana Jones
* Jurassic Park
* Lord of the Rings Trilogy
* The Shining 
* Hackers (OK, maybe it is just me that often references it...)
